settings_sources_default.python_default: setting_sources: list[SettingSource] | None = None — when None, user + project + local are ALL loaded (matches CLI defaults), including CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude settings, project skills, agents/subagents, commands and filesystem hooks.

settings_sources_default.implication: THIS OVERTURNS THE OLD REASON FOR CAUTION, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The historical 0.1.x behaviour (SDK isolated by default, CLAUDE.md/~/.claude NOT loaded unless opted in) no longer holds at these pins: the SDK now defaults to CLI-equivalent loading, so an SDK host in <adopted-project> would pick up AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude settings, project skills and filesystem hooks without extra configuration. (1) The migration friction that previously argued against the SDK is gone. (2) But the differentiator is also gone: 'same context as the CLI' is now parity, not an SDK advantage — the SDK's remaining unique value is isolation-on-demand (settingSources: []) and in-process callbacks, not context loading. (3) Caveat from the same page: settingSources does NOT control managed policy, ~/.claude.json, auto memory at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/, claude.ai MCP connectors, or sandbox credential deny/mask entries — so settingSources: [] is explicitly documented as insufficient for multi-tenant isolation.

auth_limitations.claim: The SDK's documented authentication path is an API key; subscription/claude.ai login is not the supported path and offering it is restricted.
Quickstart repeats the restriction and enumerates the supported credentials: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or third-party providers.

The restriction is scoped to 'third party developers ... for their products'; personal reuse of an existing native OAuth login by an SDK process is NOT explicitly granted or explicitly forbidden in these docs — it is undocumented. The only sentence that touches OAuth reuse indirectly is the SDK-adjacent claude.ai MCP connector row, which shows a session CAN authenticate with a claude.ai login.

For the native CLI the subscription-login behaviour IS documented: a normal (non-bare) `claude -p` run uses the subscription login; only `--bare` forces API-key auth. This is a concrete, documented advantage of the installed native CLI path for a user who signs in natively.
The installed CLI's own help states the same bare-mode auth rule, independently confirming the CLI (not bare) reads native OAuth.

result.trigger_condition: Adopt the official Claude Agent SDK ONLY when a concrete application (not the agent-lab foundation) needs one of the three things `claude -p` provably cannot do in-process, and the need is demonstrated by a failing native attempt: (a) custom tools that must execute inside the host process with shared in-memory state — e.g. a NautilusTrader engine handle, an open IBKR/Alpaca session or a live position book exposed as MCP tools via create_sdk_mcp_server(), where marshalling through an external MCP subprocess is the blocker; (b) a synchronous programmatic permission gate (can_use_tool) that must approve or deny a trade/order tool call using live in-process risk state, where --permission-prompt-tool's out-of-process MCP round-trip is unacceptable; or (c) durable session persistence outside the local filesystem (SessionStore to Redis/S3/Postgres) because the deployment target has no stable ~/.claude. Additional hard gate: the adopting component must have its own ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry credential, since the SDK's documented auth is API-key-based and this PC signs in natively by subscription OAuth. If that credential is not authorized, adoption is blocked regardless of (a)-(c).
result.overturning_comparison: This decision is overturned by any ONE of: (1) Anthropic documenting supported subscription/OAuth authentication for the Agent SDK (a primary-doc sentence replacing the current \"Use the API key authentication methods\" note at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/quickstart) — that removes the auth gap and makes the SDK a drop-in for this natively-signed-in PC; (2) the SDK exposing the Workflow tool / dynamic workflow orchestration or Agent teams as SDK options (i.e. `grep -i workflow` on a future src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py returning matches, or the claude-code-features table dropping \"Agent teams ... Not directly configured via SDK options\") — that would close the two orchestration foundation gaps; (3) a measured comparison on this machine showing a `claude -p --output-format stream-json` coordinator with bounded `--bg` workers fails or is materially slower/less reliable than an equivalent SDK host for the same agent-lab coordinator+workers+review task, with both runs' wall-clock, token usage and failure counts recorded; (4) the CLI removing or degrading a capability the SDK retains (e.g. --bg/`claude agents` lifecycle, or --permission-prompt-tool). Conversely, evidence that would HARDEN the retain-native position: the documented plan that \"--bare is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for -p in a future release\" landing, giving the CLI the SDK's isolation story by default.
result.reason: The SDK does NOT close a foundation gap for agent-lab; it is at most a conditional application dependency, and the foundation stays on the installed native CLI 2.1.278. Three independent lines of evidence: (1) CAPABILITY PARITY — every foundation primitive this harness needs is already in `claude --help` at 2.1.278 and documented at /docs/en/headless: structured JSON and stream-json (plus --json-schema structured_output), session resume/continue/fork by id or transcript path, --system-prompt/--append-system-prompt, --allowedTools/--disallowedTools/--tools/--permission-mode/--permission-prompts, --mcp-config/--strict-mcp-config, filesystem hooks with --include-hook-events, subagents via --agent/--agents with parent_tool_use_id stream attribution and --forward-subagent-text, --effort (the same five literals the SDK's EffortLevel defines: low/medium/high/xhigh/max), --model/--fallback-model, --max-budget-usd, and background worker lifecycle via --bg + `claude attach|logs|stop|rm` + `claude agents --json`. (2) THE CLI IS STRICTLY AHEAD ON ORCHESTRATION — `grep -i workflow` over the pinned Python types.py returns zero matches, and the primary docs state Agent teams are \"a CLI feature ... Not directly configured via SDK options\". The Workflow/ultracode orchestration and team coordination this project already relies on are CLI-only; moving the foundation to the SDK would LOSE capability. Likewise detached `--bg` sessions have no SDK equivalent (and -p explicitly rejects --bg, so the CLI's own detached path is the `claude --bg` + attach/logs lifecycle, not `-p --bg`). (3) AUTH — the SDK's documented credentials are ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or Bedrock/AWS/Vertex/Foundry, and claude.ai login \"for their products\" is disallowed without prior approval; this user signs in natively by subscription OAuth, which the CLI documents as working for non-bare `-p`. Adopting the SDK for foundation work would convert a working subscription path into a paid-API dependency for no capability gain. WHAT GENUINELY CHANGED SINCE THE 2026-09-21 RECORD: setting_sources/settingSources now defaults to loading user+project+local (CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude, project skills, agents, commands, filesystem hooks) — CLI-equivalent. The old \"SDK isolates by default\" objection is dead, but so is any claim that the SDK offers better project-context loading; it is now parity. The SDK's real, narrow advantages are all in-process application concerns: in-process MCP servers (McpSdkServerConfig / create_sdk_mcp_server), typed hook callbacks, can_use_tool permission callbacks, and pluggable SessionStore backends — relevant to a future NautilusTrader/broker application host, not to coordinator+workers+review+memory+RAG. PIN HYGIENE: the Python registry/release mismatch from the prior record persists unchanged (PyPI 0.2.157, newest tag v0.2.156, and `git/ref/tags/v0.2.157` 404s), so any future adoption must pin commit e9af0778559032afca55ac200608c24f18af86ca and accept that it is one patch behind the installable wheel.
